correctness.rationale: The graph/cover criterion is exact for selected and unselected pairs. Cover-one and cover-two classification checks both directions and minimality. For cover-number-three minimal solutions the two-set random-permutation argument proves at most six selected edges; the provided self-contained graph-class enumerator exhausts every isolate-free graph of one through six edges by edge-addition induction, verifies exactly four edge-critical cover-three types, and rules out K3+K2 and K4 for ordinary minimality. Direct exhaustive KG(n,2) checks for n=4..7 give 8,27,203,1029 sets and match every predicted family. Computations are inspected from the current package, and finite searches are not misrepresented as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact structural comparison: the 1993 result gives domination number three and dominating triples, while the 2023 arXiv primary source gives incidence inequalities and minimum k-tuple domination parameters. Neither asserts the five-family classification of all inclusion-minimal ordinary dominating sets or its all-size polynomial. The cover-number-three critical classification is reused as a mathematical lemma; new ordinary-domination cases include full stars, triangles, and exact proper double stars. General algorithms for enumerating minimal dominating sets do not provide the explicit Kneser count. Search failure does not imply universal priority.
residual_risks: An equivalent published classification may appear using minimal transversals, maximal irredundant families, or edge-cover criticality terminology.

value.rationale: A standard infinite graph family has a natural all-minimal domination question not determined by minimum domination or algorithmic enumeration. The complete structural family, exact labeled polynomial, upper domination number, and growing gaps form a coherent complete invariant. The cover-one/two families require independent structural reasoning and are not subsumed by total domination.
